steps.text: Require a schedulable run and --lease-id; reconcile sandbox records at startup.
Clamp active worker capacity to the run desiredWorkers and any lower --max-workers value.
Check report provenance and admit ranked candidates under the optional epoch target cap. Queue one deduplicated worker job per admitted target.
Claim each worker job and epoch target atomically. Capture base_rev once.
Provision a Daytona sandbox at that revision. Agent file access, compilation, and validation use the sandbox.
Persist checkpoints and closed worker-state evidence. The worker contract determines which checkpoint is eligible for integration.
Settle the job and clean up its sandbox. Summary and librarian consumers run only when independently enabled.
Apply eligible worker output through the serialized host integration lane. Commit accepted paths and advance the base for future claims.
Keep conflicts and failed outcomes as durable blocking evidence. The loop does not launch a conflict-resolver agent pool.
Wait for worker and integration settlement, then run the epoch boundary. Defer findings for later work instead of admitting boundary repair epochs.
Honor pause and retry outcomes. Admit the next epoch only after successful closure; update the worker base with compare-and-set.
Stop new claims and give in-flight worker jobs up to 30 seconds to settle before cancellation.
Recover interrupted active targets and await pending settlement and sandbox cleanup.
Finish an active integration drain and flush pending integration once. Await active epoch, scheduler, and knowledge-maintenance work.
Stop enabled background consumers and settle run authority through the process lifecycle. An acquired sync successor can advance after release.
